freeze_conditions: TON-IoT type unique-value inventory completed (read-only pass)
Official field/statistics documents of all three datasets reviewed
TON-IoT label semantics re-verified against official description

binary_label.role: the only mandatory cross-dataset unified label

ton_iot.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 45: 'Tag normal and attack records, where 0 indicates normal and 1 indicates attacks'

ciciot2023.rule: Benign_Final -> benign; the other 33 categories -> attack

n_baiot.rule: benign_traffic.csv -> benign; gafgyt_attacks_extracted/ and mirai_attacks_extracted/ contents -> attack
n_baiot.special_case: root-level demonstrate_structure.csv is zero-row and never enters any pipeline, so it receives no label

canonical_family.role: conservative standardized family for within-dataset multiclass and genuinely-shared cross-dataset comparison

absent_families.rule: statement of coverage, never a negative class; families are never forced into an 'other' bucket for alignment

fixed_decisions.rule: Gafgyt tcp/udp are NOT re-labelled as ddos; Gafgyt scan is NOT merged into recon; malware family and behavior type are different axes. A separate behavior_tag may be added later if evidence supports it but never replaces canonical_family.

canonical_family.note: Final family assignments are NOT frozen until the TON-IoT type inventory is complete and official documents are reviewed.

ton_iot_type_mapping.description: Mapping of the 9 TON-IoT attack type values plus normal to canonical_family. All entries carry decision_status=proposed; none are frozen yet.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 45 (label=0 -> normal) + row 46 (type=normal); TON-IoT label census: 50,000 rows with label=0 and type=normal
entries.rationale: Direct 1:1 mapping; verified invariant: all label=0 rows have type=normal and vice versa (census confirmed zero exceptions). This is a coverage invariant, not one of the 9 attack classes.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists backdoor as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 backdoor rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Backdoor is a distinct attack class with unique semantics (covert channel / unauthorized remote access). No existing candidate family subsumes it; expanding the family list rather than forcing it into another bucket.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists DDoS as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 ddos rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Distributed Denial-of-Service is a well-established attack family distinct from single-source DoS by the distributed source characteristic. CICIoT2023 also has a DDoS category, enabling genuine cross-dataset comparison at this family level.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists DoS as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 dos rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Denial-of-Service from a single source is semantically distinct from DDoS (distributed). Both TON-IoT and CICIoT2023 carry DoS as a separate category; keeping them separate preserves this distinction.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists injection as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 injection rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Injection attacks (SQL injection, code injection, command injection) form a distinct technical family targeting data/code integrity. Not subsumable under web_attack because injection can occur on non-HTTP channels. Expanded as an independent family.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists password as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 password rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Password attacks (brute-force, credential stuffing, password guessing) are a distinct attack family targeting authentication. Not subsumable under backdoor (which implies established covert access, not the credential-cracking phase). Expanded as an independent family.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists ransomware as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 ransomware rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Ransomware is a distinct attack family characterized by encryption/extortion payload behavior. Its network-level signature differs from other attack families. Expanded as an independent family; not subsumable under any existing candidate.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists scanning as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 scanning rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Scanning is a reconnaissance activity (probing for open ports, services, vulnerabilities). Mapped to canonical_family=recon because scanning is the behavioral manifestation of reconnaissance. This is a derived mapping (source_type name differs from canonical_family name); the semantic link is well-established in IDS literature. Note: this does NOT merge Gafgyt scan into recon — that is a malware family subtype on a different axis.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists xss as an attack category; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 20,000 xss rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is a web-application-layer attack. Mapped to canonical_family=web_attack as a broader family that encompasses XSS and other web-based exploits. This is a derived mapping (specific XSS -> general web_attack). CICIoT2023 also has a Web-based category, enabling potential cross-dataset comparison at this family level.

entries.evidence_source: Network Features-Description.pdf row 46 lists attack categories including normal, DoS, DDoS and backdoor attacks; Statistics of Network Records.pdf lists 1,043 mitm rows in train/test
entries.rationale: Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) is a distinct attack family involving traffic interception/relay. It is not subsumable under any existing candidate family. The 1,043-row count is a natural imbalance point (the only attack class below 20,000), not an error. Expanded as an independent family.

coverage_invariant.rule: normal -> benign must hold for all rows; all label=0 rows must have type=normal and vice versa
coverage_invariant.evidence_source: TON-IoT label census (TON-IOT-LABEL-CENSUS-20260903-V1-VERIFIED): 50,000 label=0 rows all have type=normal; 161,043 label=1 rows all have type in {backdoor,ddos,dos,injection,password,ransomware,scanning,xss,mitm}; zero exceptions

source_subtype.role: official original labels, verbatim; never a cross-dataset unified task

per_dataset.n_baiot: family directory + CSV filename, verbatim, stored as source_family and source_subtype

grouping_metadata.role: provenance and group-aware splits only; never model features

notes.capture_id: CICIoT2023: filename stem (e.g. DDoS-ACK_Fragmentation12); N-BaIoT: device+family+subtype triple; TON-IoT: not available in the selected train_test_network.csv

ton_iot.label_location: label column (0/1) + type column (attack subtype string)

special_case.location: root of the extracted tree, not inside any device directory
special_case.disposition: retained in frozen inventory as shipped; never enters training, evaluation, or label assignment
